articles.title: The Wildest New Foods in NBA Arenas This Season
articles.summary: Another NBA season is upon us.
articles.body:
For some fans, that means hoping their team finally breaks out of mediocrity and ascends to the playoffs. For a lucky few, it's a victory lap after a thrilling Finals victory.

But for anyone actually planning to attend a game this season, it's the start of a pilgrimage to try the weirdest new foods their arenas offer for the 2026–27 season.

As social media trends continue to push food and beverage trends into more and more unhinged territory, NBA arenas are among many bar and restaurant programs competing to create the next viral food item. (Short rib corn dog, anyone?)

Here are the weirdest ones you can find around the U.S. this season.

American Airlines Center (Dallas Mavericks): Crunchy Sweet Corn Fritters

Everything's bigger in Texas—including the appetite for state-fair-style food.

It makes sense. Dallas is home to the State Fair of Texas, where figuring out what to deep-fry next has practically become a competitive sport.

At American Airlines Center, the Mavericks have submitted their own offering: Crunchy Sweet Corn Fritters by Loro, the Asian smokehouse and bar co-founded by chef Tyson Cole and Aaron Franklin, as part of its arena concessions residency.

Though Texas is situated outside of the traditional Midwest "Corn Belt," corn has deep roots in Texas, making this gameday snack even more apropos.

Fiserv Forum (Milwaukee Bucks): Campfire Funnel Fries

In a state that spends as much time outside as Wisconsinites do, it makes sense that the home of the Milwaukee Bucks would bring the great outdoors courtside.

This season, Fiserv Forum is serving up Campfire Funnel Fries: warm funnel fries piled with marshmallow cream, chocolate sauce, cinnamon sugar and graham cracker crumbles.

It's everything you love about a gooey campfire s'more, minus the smoke, the sticky marshmallow stick and—for most of basketball season in Wisconsin—the below-freezing temperatures.

Intuit Dome (L.A. Clippers): Poke Nachos

If there's any arena in the country you would trust to prepare raw fish for you, it would almost certainly be in Los Angeles.

At the L.A. Clippers' Intuit Dome, poke nachos are new for 2026 and feature fresh bigeye tuna with spicy mayo, green onion, sesame seeds and crispy wonton chips.

This isn't the first Intuit Dome item to feature raw fish; it's simply the latest. Previously, the arena unveiled a spicy tuna "sushi dog," which was described as being "like a sushi burrito in the size and portability of a hot dog."

The new poke nachos can be found at Pick & Roll and Fast Break markets.

Overreacting to every NBA team's first game

Kaseya Center (Miami Heat): Caviar Latkes

Miami is synonymous with luxury, so it stands to reason that the high-end indulgence wouldn't stop at the doors of Kaseya Center.

At Heat games this season, fans can find Caviar Latkes, which offer a decadent spin on a comfort-food staple. Crispy potato latkes come topped with caviar, shallot, chopped egg and crème fraiche, giving a humble classic a South Beach glow-up. Whether you're ordering them to your seat or enjoying them in one of the arena's swanky lounges, these are not your bubbe's potato pancakes.

As a bonus, if you've been looking at the calendar for a reason to convince your family to celebrate Hanukkah at the Heat game, consider this your sign.

Kia Center (Orlando Magic): Hot Honey Chicken Sub

Publix, the Florida-born supermarket chain that opened its first store in Winter Haven in 1930, has practically cornered the market on chicken tender subs, affectionately known as PubSubs among its devoted fan base. So it's only fitting that Orlando's Kia Center is getting in on the action this season.

Magic fans can find the Hot Honey Chicken Sub in two 100-level sections at Kia Center. The sandwich features crispy chicken tenders coated in hot honey and topped with house-made blue cheese coleslaw.

Moda Center (Portland Trail Blazers): Elote Mini Corn Dog Nachos

Every word of this menu item is a surprise, yet it just keeps getting more unhinged.

At Portland's Moda Center this season, the Trail Blazers are serving Elote Mini Corn Dog Nachos, a concession-stand fever dream that dared to ask, What if an NBA game was held at the state fair and also somehow a gas station?

Mini corn dog bites are topped with roasted street corn, creamy chipotle mayo, cotija cheese, fresh cilantro, Tajín and Flamin' Hot Cheetos dust. Subtlety has left the building.

Paycom Center (OKC Thunder): Chicken Fried Steak Sandwich

Chicken-fried steak isn't just an Oklahoma comfort-food favorite; it's actually part of the official state meal . In 1988, the Oklahoma Legislature bestowed that honor upon it, along with barbecue pork, sausage and biscuits with gravy, cornbread, fried okra, black-eyed peas, strawberries and pecan pie.

It's really three official meals—breakfast, lunch and dinner—and you can satisfy one of them at Thunder games this season with Paycom Center's new Chicken Fried Steak Sandwich.

The stick-to-your-ribs item features chicken-fried steak topped with Tabasco onions, black-pepper house gravy and bread-and-butter pickles on a brioche bun, served with fries.

Rocket Arena (Cleveland Cavaliers): Birria Eggroll

One of the trickiest parts of attending an NBA game is wrangling your food and drink as you attempt to find your seat on a 35-degree slope 75 feet in the air. While the trend lately in arena food innovation has been "bigger is better" (see: the Pittsburgh Penguins' new 14-pound deli sandwich ), some chefs understand fans just need something portable.

This is where the humble eggroll shines. The vehicle is perfect: loose fillings are safely secured inside a crispy, hermetically sealed shell. In Rocket Arena's new creation, those fillings include birria and Chihuahua cheese. The birria eggroll is also served with a lime wedge and a customary rich consommé for dipping.

Rocket Arena notes that the concoction is only available for a limited time, so keep an eye out for it when you attend your first Cavs game this season.

State Farm Arena (Atlanta Hawks): Dirty Soda

There's no question that dirty soda has reached obsession status in the U.S. From brick-and-mortar shops to mobile trucks to movie theaters and sports arenas, the fizzy, syrupy, creamy concoctions can be found across almost all 50 states.

However, when they're served as part of a menu lineup in quick-service environments such as movie theaters and arenas, dirty sodas are often premade directly from the fountain (think: Dirty Mountain Dew). So it's notable that State Farm Arena is offering four craft dirty sodas made to order.

The lineup includes Peaches & Cream (Sprite with sweet peach syrup, vanilla and a splash of sweet cream); the All-Star (Coke with coconut syrup, fresh lime juice and sweet cream), the Creamsicle (Orange Fanta with vanilla and sweet cream) and the Shark Attack (Sprite with blue curaçao syrup, grenadine and sweet cream).

TD Garden (Boston Celtics): Beer Sneaker

The hottest concessions items in 2026 are not food at all; they're unique vessels out of which to consume liquids (most often, beer).

Hockey has really gotten the jump on this trend. The Carolina Hurricanes have had a viral Beer Skate, the Buffalo Sabres have offered a Beer Sabre, and the Utah Mammoth contributed a Tusk Mug. The Boston Celtics' TD Garden roommates, the Boston Bruins, will debut a Beer Glove this season, and now the Celtics themselves are joining the trend with a Beer Sneaker.

The visionary plastic vessel, shaped like a classic Chuck Taylor All-Star sneaker, features green shoelaces and a Celtics logo.

The sneaker costs $24 and comes filled with draft beer of your choice. Maybe we've become numb to inflation-era pricing, because that seems like a great deal.

Xfinity Mobile Arena (Philadelphia 76ers): Short Rib Corn Dog

When it comes to the trend of mixing culinary highs and lows in the U.S., Philadelphia has always been at the forefront. From Roxanne's dinosaur chicken nuggets served with crème fraîche and caviar to wagyu cheesesteaks topped with cheese from a can, Philly understands that food shouldn't take itself too seriously.

That mentality is perfectly on display in the new Short Rib Corn Dog offering at Xfinity Mobile Arena this season.

The short rib fried into the corndog is the same high-end meat served at Primepoint Social, the members-only club-level restaurant inside the arena. But the general public can get it on the concourse mezzanine level.

articles.title: Power Ranking Every NBA Team's Starting Lineup
articles.summary: NBA coaches will swear up and down that it's not about which players start but which players finish games.
articles.body:
NBA coaches will swear up and down that it's not about which players start but which players finish games.

Our well-reasoned, rational, wholly mature response: Psshhh!

OK, so closing games is actually a big deal, but starting them is, too. It's a big honor, for one, and clearly a point of pride. Not to mention, coaches obviously want their teams to get off to a good start, so it means quite a bit being one of the five players tasked with getting that done.

The (very) early portion of the 2026-27 season has given us glimpses of how teams will deploy their starters, so let's break down and rank every team's starting lineup based on fit, talent, production and potential.

These rankings assess each team's expected starting lineup, including regular starters who missed opening night, rather than strictly the five players who started its opener.

The Bucks were forced to trade away their best player in franchise history this offseason, and the package of players they brought back offers more quantity than quality.

Herro has technically been an All-Star, but shooting is his lone standout skill. He's a solid support scorer and secondary playmaker, but handing him the offensive keys is usually asking for disappointment.

Then again, it's not like Milwaukee has obvious alternatives.

Rollins impressed last season, but he's had one year of posting big numbers on a bad team. Kuzma and Turner are veteran holdovers who are seemingly waiting for any win-now shopper to take an interest. Jaquez is...fine, but maybe mostly in a he-can-pilot-your-second-unit kind of way.

It's a good thing Bulls fans can spend much of this season imagining all of the fun that might be part of a future led by Wilson and Buzelis. Because this could be a pretty rough watch in the present.

Powell gets over his skis as a primary scorer. He also might be the only quantity-plus-quality shooter in this quintet. Giddey could be more of a compiler than an actual contributor. Wilson's tools are special, but his offensive game is raw. Buzelis took a big leap as a sophomore, but averaging 16.3 points and 2.1 assists on a 51-loss team isn't exactly moving the needle. Claxton was just deemed non-essential by a Brooklyn Nets team with pretty underwhelming options at the 5.

Could these Bulls make a charge to their 30-something-win comfort zone? Maybe, but their (overdue) acceptance of a rebuild seems likelier to usher in the kind of losing typically associated with a top-to-bottom reset.

Admittedly, the Kings probably don't have the league's third-least talented starting five. Sabonis and LaVine have five All-Star selections between them, and Acuff was just the seventh player selected in one of the better regarded drafts in recent memory.

That said, this is very much a franchise in flux. Sacramento would love to unload both of those former stars if it could ever find a taker, so it could lean into a youth movement and eventually get things on the right track. But given their contract commitments and reputations as regular-season compilers, the Kings might have to incentivize trade partners to take either off their hands.

So, this team—and this lineup—is stuck between multiple, in some ways directly competing timelines. The Kings need to showcase the vets to hopefully increase their value, which limits the chances for someone like Acuff to find his footing. And, frankly, the less said about Hunter and Murray (who combined to have eight points on 13 shots in the opener), the better.

Overreacting to every NBA team's first game

Every NBA Team's Top 3 Trade Targets This Season 🎯

Not to kick the Clippers while they're down, but the long-term consequences of the NBA's salary-cap penalties could linger for years. On the court, those sanctions did little to change this season's outlook, which, as this ranking reflects, looks pretty grim.

Things should at least get better whenever Brandon Ingram is ready to return from May surgery on a right heel injury and partially torn Achilles tendon. And things should get more entertaining if rookie first-rounder Keaton Wagler ever wrestles away Dunn's starting spot.

For now, though, it's sort of just Garland on an island with a slew of unspectacular veterans around him. For as creative as Garland is and as potent as he can be, scoring could be an absolute grind for this group.

Props to the Grizzlies for giving Wells the starting nod over veteran newcomer Jerami Grant. Not to slight Grant or anything—he is, at worst, a solid, starting-level player—but this seems to reflect an accurate assessment that this club's future towers over its present in importance.

And, hey, maybe this starting unit can help Memphis have a pretty promising present as is. Especially if Jerome has more fire-breathing efforts like his 45-point, six-assist, five-triple showing in the opener.

Boozer is an absurdly advanced processor for a teenaged rookie, Coward and Wells are helpful dot-connectors and Edey is a 7'4", 305-pound mountain of a man who can control the interior. The Grizzlies could become something pretty special down the line, but they can open a few eyes already this season, too.

Between Fears, Murray and Williamson, the Pels shouldn't be hurting for on-ball creativity. And with trade-market superstar Murphy in the mix, this is a group that could pile up points.

They do know, though, that defense is a part of the game, too, right? Because crowning Fears and Murray both winners of their training camp battle for a starting guard spot left this group without shutdown stopper Herbert Jones.

Maybe the trade-off will be worth it, but if the plan is to simply overwhelm opponents with offense, then it might need the most efficient versions of these players to date. Because this group could bleed points on the perimeter, and the paint protection might be just as flimsy.

Consider this rating a bit of a shoulder shrug for this group. It's not that the Nets totally lack talent; it's that it's a little hard to figure out how Brooklyn plans to blend high-scoring veterans Porter and Randle with such a youth-heavy roster.

The fact that the Nets started Ellis over No. 6 pick Mikel Brown Jr. suggests they might put more of a premium on competing over development, though it could have more to do with the ankle injury that limited Brown in the preseason.

Then again, Ellis' three-and-D game might be easier to plug into this lineup considering how many touches will be taken up by Porter and Randle, and Brown should have more on-ball chances with the second unit.

Unless the Nets think Porter and Randle are legitimate building blocks, though, there is at least some worry those two will monopolize possessions and leave players more important to the franchise's future lacking opportunities to grow.

In Brooklyn's season opener—a loss to a Kon Knueppel-less, Coby White-less Charlotte team—Porter and Randle accounted for 39 of the starters' 61 field-goal attempts.

This Charlotte fivesome has a chance to be pretty fun. Maybe not peak LaMelo Ball turning NBA games into AAU runs kind of fun, but a fun brand of basketball where the ball zips around and finds capable shooters at most spots.

This ranking is placing a slight wager on some internal growth, but this lineup isn't lacking for potential improvers. Knueppel had a historic shooting run as a rookie, Miller can look the part of a star big wing (the most coveted archetype in basketball) and Reid could really blossom with more of a featured role than he filled in Minnesota.

There will still be questions about Knueppel and Miller as first and second options, and those will be important questions since this is built to be an offense-forward group.

This lineup looks like—well, a bummer, to be honest. Curry is a magical basketball force, obviously, but he just doesn't have the kind of support he deserves for his twilight years.

If someone could magic-wand Jimmy Butler, Kristaps Porziņģis (a super-early trade candidate ) and Moses Moody back to full strength, maybe things would be different, but these Dubs will be depleted for a while.

And it's already showing. Granted, Golden State was without Podziemski (back) on opening night, but Curry's lack of support loomed as a fatal flaw. He netted 23 points; no other Warrior had even 15. Newcomer Brandon Williams came closest with 14 off the bench—while misfiring on nine of his 12 field-goal attempts.

Curry's presence alone keeps the Warriors from falling any farther, but this is about as bleak as it gets for a generational great. Hopefully, the Warriors at least avoid a total collapse amid their injury issues, because a full-strength starting lineup would probably push for top-10 status.

If Suns fans want to know why external trade speculation around Booker exists despite Phoenix's steadfast refusal to even entertain the idea, you might be looking at it. He is clearly without a co-star, and this lineup lacks some of the basic things the Suns probably need to win anything of substance.

Like, where is the offensive organizer? Or the space-creating shooters? Who can consistently be relied upon for paint protection and rebounding? In the season-opener, the Suns' starters shot 3-of-13 from range, assisted on only six of their 19 field goals and lost the rebounding battle 27-20.

Green and Bridges are volume scorers, Brooks is a defensive stopper and Maluach is unproven at this level. The sum of the parts still adds up to a non-terrible ranking, but the whole shows too many holes for these five to climb any higher.

Hopes are high for the Irving-Flagg pairing— for however long it lasts . Not in a Dallas-could-be-sneaky-awesome kind of way, but definitely in the sense that Irving's creation, scoring, playmaking and experience could all make life easier on Flagg.

That part of this equation seems promising. It's the other three spots preventing the Mavs from entering the teens.

Christie, Washington and Gafford are all fine. That's just too many replaceable parts in a five-man lineup. Especially with Irving being a 34-year-old returning after a season-plus on the sidelines (ACL), and Flagg being just a 19-year-old sophomore.

There are certainly scenarios in which the Jazz could make this ranking look low. Jackson and Markkanen have All-Star trips on their resumes, George had All-Star-ish numbers last season and Peterson was often regarded as the top talent in a loaded 2026 draft class.

That being said, Markkanen and George have posted their best numbers on some brutally bad teams. Jackson's offense lacks consistency, and his defense still features too many fouls and not enough rebounds. Peterson's best film came back in high school. It's both reasonable and rational to question this club's ability to immediately flip the switch after consecutive 60-loss seasons.

Utah's season-opener was rough , but it was missing Nurkić. Then again, the 32-year-old non-star center wasn't exactly the reason for preseason optimism around this team.

Did any combo up its stock more in its season opener than the Blazers' new backcourt? Sure, it's only one game, and the Suns looked awful , but this is exactly how believers in the Morant-Lillard backcourt hoped it would look: 39 points on 13-of-20 shooting (8-of-13 from range) and 14 assists against two turnovers.

"You only get one chance at a first impression," Morant told reporters . "And that was our message to each other before we ran out of the tunnel, to make sure we leave a good message and start off on the right foot."

One game, of course, hardly defines anything, and there are clearly questions of durability, shot distribution and backcourt defense. If shots are falling, though, this group gives the Blazers the chance to start out with a flurry before coach Micah Nori starts mixing and matching the on-court configurations to balance things out.

The Wizards make you want to believe, because their best-case scenarios are wildly entertaining. And, honestly, this ranking indicates at least some level of belief given that this franchise has delivered three consecutive 64-plus-loss seasons.

Granted, Davis and Dybantsa played in exactly none of those seasons, and Young was only slightly more involved (five appearances), but the stench from that level of losing can sometimes linger. If nothing else, the lack of meaningful basketball made it impossible to gauge whether George or Sarr could contribute to a winner.

Will the Wizards get a total buy-in from Davis given the lack of established talent around him? Are they built the right way to capitalize on Young's offensive gifts and minimize his defensive deficiencies? Is Dybantsa the kind of top pick who can star right away, or will he need some time to blossom? We don't know those answers, but we're eager to find out.

If this assessed only talent in a vacuum, the Magic might push for a top-10 placement. Wagner and Banchero are certified stars, Bane is one of the Association's best third options and Suggs and Carter are helpful to have at both ends.

So, why can't Orlando crack the upper half? Because basketball isn't played in a vacuum. The puzzle pieces have to fit, and there's just too much overlap—Wagner and Banchero both work best on the ball; Bane is the only reliable shooter—to trust they ever will.

An upgraded primary playmaker might better balance all the mouths to feed. A shooting upgrade or two could give everyone more breathing room. This fivesome doesn't feel that far away, but an internal breakthrough will be tricky to engineer.

The Lakers spent this offseason retrofitting their roster around Dončić. Their starting lineup doesn't necessarily reflect that.

It has his long-awaited rim-runner in Kessler and a good amount of wing defense to cover for the backcourt's limitations on that end. It is short on shooting, though, as the guards are the lone sources of either volume or efficiency from distance. Starters not named Dončić went just 3-of-7 from range in Wednesday's opener.

This still might work. L.A. could get all of the shooting it needs out of its guards, and Dončić can fashion Kessler into a legitimate offensive weapon (26 points, 12-of-12 from the field in his Lakers' debut). It still has a worrisome amount of one-way players, though.

The Celtics probably lost their shot at contention after trading away Jaylen Brown this summer. They still have a chance to factor into the Eastern Conference race, though, provided Tatum rediscovers his old superstar form.

If Tatum is a clear-cut elite, this lineup can cover most bases behind him. George is a little shaky as a second option at his age (36), but White will help with that role most nights. Having two non-spacers in the lineup seems strange for a Joe Mazzulla squad, but Walsh's versatility and Robinson's blend of length and bounce are major defensive assets.

There isn't a ton of safety net should Tatum struggle at all in his first full season back from a torn Achilles or should George show his age, but the high-end outcomes here are still pretty good.

The Heat are hard to handle here. On one hand, it's really hard to doubt Erik Spoelstra's ability to maximize a roster with a superstar centerpiece (Antetokounmpo) and a legitimate co-star (Adebayo). On the other, it's a little too easy to wonder whether Antetokounmpo has any more scoring help than he did in Milwaukee.

Adebayo isn't your classic No. 2 option. Thompson was at one point, but age and injuries have relegated him to shooting-specialist duties. Wiggins looks like a second option some nights, but he can be invisible on others. Mitchell is a low-volume scorer and shooter who Miami hopes just provides passable playmaking.

All of that said, Antetokounmpo is awesome, and so is Spo, and Adebayo is good-to-great at a lot of different things. Leaving that trio out of the top 10 seems risky, but concerns around spacing, creation and perimeter scoring left us no choice.

This lineup has just about everything you'd want in a starting five. Well, everything other than a superstar, and we're high enough in the rankings now that the lack of a true elite talent looms pretty large.

Johnson took a big leap last season, but that final climb from really good to great is the hardest to traverse. He would need to up his scoring output and widen his range to scale it.

Even if he doesn't, though, there's lots to like with how these pieces all fit. This lineup was comically dominant last season ( plus-20.3 over 391 minutes), but it was enough of a mess in the playoffs ( minus-14.4 across 82 minutes) to wonder if it played high above its head.

Game 1 of Leonard's second stint up north played out about exactly as expected—provided you expected big things from this group, of course. The offense was balanced (and largely focused inside the arc), the defense was swarming and Poeltl was the least convincing (or impactful) member of the opening quintet.

The other four Raptors starters all scored 20-plus points. They all had multiple assists, too, and collectively dished 12 dimes against just a single turnover. They all had opportunities to contribute offensively (though Chicago didn't exactly provide the most defensive resistance).

It'd be nice if there was more shooting here, and you wonder whether Barrett can be his best self with perhaps fewer touches. The Leonard-Barnes combo could be special, though, and if the backcourt is merely above-average, the Raptors could be in business.

Four of these players—everyone but Collins—filled a starting spot for last season's 60-win Pistons and comprised one of the better high-mileage quartets in basketball. Cunningham, Robinson, Thompson and Duren spent 699 minutes together and outscored opponents by 11 points per 100 possessions.

That level of success matters. Yes, even if the shooting looks a little light, and there still isn't a second-creator in the mix. In fact, they lost some creation in their first five with Collins replacing Tobias Harris.

But Cunningham is an MVP candidate, Duren is a capable All-Star, Thompson is an All-Galaxy defender and Robinson is a top-shelf net-shredder. Collins has a chance to shine as a play-finisher, too. These five have some warts, but they have plenty of clear and compelling strengths.

Haliburton lost all of last season to the Achilles tear that forced him out of Game 7 of the 2025 NBA Finals (a championship trip he booked while starting alongside Nembhard, Nesmith and Siakam). During the Pacers' opener, Haliburton showed zero signs of rust, netting 23 points on 15 shots and dishing 12 assists against three giveaways.

If Haliburton can play at an All-NBA level, then Indiana might need to rank even higher. Again, the only change from that Finals group is swapping in Zubac for Myles Turner, which sacrifices spacing but gains plenty of interior oomph, rebounding and finishing.

The Rockets failed to launch last season. On a directly related note, they played the entire campaign without their primary offensive organizer, VanVleet.

Well, VanVleet is back now, and their offense looked very much organized and energized in their opener. He had 11 assists in 30 turnover-free minutes, and the other four starters all had 16-plus points on 50-plus percent shooting, led by 30 apiece from Durant and Smith.

The offense won't always operate at peak efficiency, but the scoring punch is so powerful, that it can net a bunch of points on less than perfect nights. There are a couple of soft spots in the defense, but there's also tons of length, mobility and disruption.

When the Timberwolves brokered a bold blockbuster trade for Ball, they immediately assembled something: if not the best backcourt in the NBA, then certainly the most entertaining.

Edwards being able to toggle between scoring and table-setting responsibilities might be a cheat code. Ball being second in the scoring pecking order might usher in even more playmaking from a player who already ranks among the Association's premier passers.

With so much defensive attention paid to these guards, McDaniels and Kuminga can feast on open shots. That may not leave many touches for Gobert (two shots in 33 minutes in their opener), but that also might allow him to funnel even more energy into his defense and rebounding.

The Cavaliers have a lot riding on Watson being their missing-piece answer at small forward. If they haven't cracked the championship code with this move, it might mean rethinking the core four foundation of this roster.

This placement sort of hedges that bet. It certainly allows for the chance for Cleveland to be great, but it stops well short of guaranteeing that will happen.

More simply, it paints a pretty clear picture of just how much talent Cleveland has collected. Mitchell is an offensive megastar, Harden is a nightly threat for a 20-point, 10-dime double-double and the Mobley-Allen combo can cover up a lot of the backcourt's defensive weaknesses. Watson might be Cleveland's stingiest small forward yet, and hopefully the 24-year-old can build upon his 2025-26 offensive breakout (14.6 points per game, 41.1 three-point percentage).

It is, without question, concerning how often the Nuggets are allowing solid starters to walk out the door for economic reasons. It's also probably not nearly as problematic as it would be without the presence of Jokić, who may still hold the title of best player on the planet.

He's just such a dynamic problem-solver as a 6'11", 284-pound playmaker who doubles as a near-30-point scorer on unfair shooting efficiency that you can only doubt anything about Denver so much. Even the clear weak spots here (Braun and Johnson) feel like they could morph into strengths, based somewhat on their track records but more so on how often Jokić will position them for success.

Defense could be a mess, especially if Gordon's recent availability issues resurface, but the offense might be so prolific that it doesn't matter. Braun and Johnson both had disappointing 2025-26 seasons, and this quintet still poured in an absurd 127 points per 100 possessions.

Leaning into this three-guard lineup has allowed the Spurs to find more shared floor time for their most talented players. It has also exposed them to obvious concerns regarding overlap, fit and role redundancy.

You still have to respect the talent, and this ranking does. Between the perimeter speed and Wembanyama's strength, San Antonio can cause chaos on the defensive end, which can directly fuel its dynamic transition attack. Offense can get clunkier in the half-court, but defenses are kept off-balance by the presence of so many playmakers and scoring threats.

It will take time for everything to jell, and it's possible the Spurs could just pull the plug at some point (to improve the spacing or even spark up the second unit if it's lagging way behind). But if things ever fully click, this is a lineup that could routinely dismantle opponents at both ends of the floor.

Wait, wasn't this lineup just responsible for snapping New York's 53-year championship drought? And didn't it pulverize opponents by 12.5 points per 100 possessions in the playoffs? Why isn't it a lock at No. 1?

Well, before that postseason surge, it was more pretty good than great ( plus-2.3 net rating). And that probably aligns closer to realistic expectations. Brunson is awesome, but he's not part of the best-on-the-planet discussions, and this lineup lacks offensive consistency around him. All five players are capable scorers, but everyone not named Bridges can frustratingly disappear at times.

It's still the backbone of a champion, impresses with both star power and balance and lacks an obvious weakness. Sitting third overall says less about what this lineup can and can't do and more about how stacked the top two really is.

By track record, this lineup should probably sit No. 1. It'll get there on the eye test for plenty of observers, too. The puzzle pieces are brilliant in their own right and museum-worthy once connected. The Thunder somehow manage to make full use of their impressive depth while also letting SGA's star shine as bright as possible.

There's just this harmonious lockstep in everything the Thunder do. Gilgeous-Alexander pilots everything, but he'll share the controls if someone else has it rolling. And if they don't, the role players will just lean into whatever duties best help the team.

There are still a few swing factors that could bump this group to No. 1 or perhaps drop it down a few spots. Can Williams get back to an All-Star level after an injury-riddled season? Does Holmgren have another gear on the offensive end? And what does Wallace provide as the unit's newest member other than dogged defense?

The unknowns carry copious amounts of excitement, and maybe they'll play a part in helping this club recapture its championship form. Still, that's enough uncertainty to slot this team just behind our fully loaded lineup in the No. 1 spot.

This is one of the most loaded lineups—on paper—in recent memory. You'd have trouble assembling this much talent in an NBA2K27 franchise mode, at least without turning off the salary cap and turning on trade override.

James is a four-time MVP and a reasonable response in the GOAT debate. The last time Embiid was healthy, he won the scoring title and the MVP. Maxey made All-NBA third-team last season; Brown made All-NBA second-team and received MVP votes. Edgecombe, easily the least decorated of the lot, snagged a spot on an All-Rookie first-team that's overloaded with star potential.

The offensive hierarchy could take a while to get sorted. The defense could run into issues (especially against athletic frontcourts). The spacing could get tight at times. The durability concerns attached to Embiid (96 games played the last three seasons combined) and James (turns 42 in December) are obvious and maybe ominous.

And yet, all of that pales in comparison to this unrivaled collection of established, elite talent. When assessing five-man lineups, it's hard not to marvel at the one featuring four different stars and an energetic, explosive 21-year-old with gobs of untapped potential.

articles.title: Blockbuster Trade Idea To Blow Up the 2026-27 NBA Season
articles.summary: We're less than a week into the 2026-27 NBA season, but the trade rumor mill never stops churning. And it got an influx of water with this week's news that the Golden State Warriors might be mulling over Kristaps Porziņģis trades.
articles.body:
We're less than a week into the 2026-27 NBA season, but the trade rumor mill never stops churning. And it got an influx of water with this week's news that the Golden State Warriors might be mulling over Kristaps Porziņģis trades.

With KP's Postural Orthostatic Tachycardia Syndrome (POTS) diagnosis unfortunately threatening his career and the careful construction of his current contract by the Warriors, he could essentially be a trade exception.

His 2026-27 salary is $20 million, and his contract is only guaranteed for another $3 million in 2027-28. A team looking for some financial flexibility (or to get out of their own cumbersome deal) could be interested in taking on Porziņģis, paying that $20 million this year and then eating the small guarantee to get out of the deal over the summer.

And if the Warriors were willing to pair him with a franchise legend (who's on an actual expiring contract) and take one more gamble for the sake of Stephen Curry, the New Orleans Pelicans may have exactly the kind of player who could give him one last shot a title.

Pelicans Receive: Draymond Green, Kristaps Porziņģis and a top-four protected 2027 first-round pick

Again, this is a gamble. And Warriors fans will certainly quibble with a pick going out in this deal.

But the cap math works, and we'll explain why both teams should be interested below.

Trading one health risk for another is not ideal. Surrendering a precious draft asset in the process makes it even less so. And prior to recent news on Porziņģis, Zion was arguably the biggest health risk in the league (with tongue-in-cheek apologies to KP and Joel Embiid).

But in this point in their careers, Zion would represent a massive talent upgrade over Draymond. And whatever that swap would cost Golden State defensively, Williamson could offset it on the other end.

When healthy (a caveat thrown around a lot, but always feels necessary in his case), Zion remains one of the most devastating interior scorers of all time. Among players wtih at least as many career minutes, Williamson's career average of 27.8 points per 75 possessions trails only Joel Embiid (31.6), Luka Dončić (30.6) and Michael Jordan (30.3).

The fact that he does so much of his damage inside the three-point line would make him a dynamic pairing with Curry. Zion has real gravity in the paint. Curry obviously has it from beyond the arc.

The push-and-pull they'd force on opposing defenses—especially once Jimmy Butler is back to facilitate—could once again give Golden State one of the NBA's most dangerous offenses.

Of course, they'd still be a long shot to even finish in the top six in the West and a longer one to seriously threaten the contenders. But right now, the Warriors are a "no shot" team, and it just feels wrong for that to be true of a team with Curry.

The logic on this side is a lot simpler.

New Orleans has only made the playoffs twice since Zion was drafted. It was eliminated in the first round both years, and Zion didn't play in either of those series.

He simply hasn't worked out as the face of the franchise. And now, the Pelicans have a couple of other candidates to fill that role in Derik Queen and Jeremiah Fears.

This deal gets them out of the Zion contract set to pay him $44.9 million next season without taking on any other big money. It also shifts the team toward Queen and Fears and gives it an asset to build around them.

It'd make even more sense if they added to that asset cache with moves involving Trey Murphy, Dejounte Murray and Herb Jones, too. But the Pelicans have to start somewhere.

articles.title: Jaylen Brown Calls 'Cap' on Jayson Tatum for His Reaction to 76ers Trade in Trending Video
articles.summary: Jaylen Brown is seemingly not convinced his former Boston Celtics star teammate Jayson Tatum really had a shocked and emotional reaction to his offseason trade to the Philadelphia 76ers.
articles.body:
Jaylen Brown is seemingly not convinced his former Boston Celtics star teammate Jayson Tatum really had a shocked and emotional reaction to his offseason trade to the Philadelphia 76ers.

Brown responded to a clip of Tatum discussing his response to learning Brown had been traded with a cap emoji.

Tatum said in a video posted Thursday to his YouTube Channel he was "just as much caught off guard as the rest of the world" by the Brown trade.

He claimed he had first learned about the deal when ESPN reporter Shams Charania approached him after a pickup game in Las Vegas.

"Shams walks over," Tatum said. "He hands me the towel. He's like, 'Yo, put this over your face. Don't react. They just traded him.'"

"I'm like, 'Oh, s--t.' I'm like, 'Where?' He said, 'Philly.' I said, 'We traded him down the street?'"

Tatum went on to say it had always been "me and JB" throughout their decade-long tenure with the Celtics.

"Every time I stepped on the court, that when it was time to go to war, I looked to my left and my right, and No. 7 was over there, I knew that he was going to do everything it took for us to try to win," Tatum said.

"The way we pushed each other, I definitely made him better, and he made me better. And we made our team better, we made the organization better. We won a championship. We are forever stitched in stone in NBA history. We held up that trophy. It won't ever be forgotten."

Charania reported shortly after the Brown trade he and Tatum had a "non-existent" personal relationship off the court prior to the move.

The Brown trade sent Paul George and two first-round picks to Boston and ultimately played a role in drawing LeBron James to Philadelphia.

He made his Sixers debut Tuesday night with a season-opening win over the defending champion New York Knicks, while Tatum is still searching for his first victory of the post-Brown era after losing to the Detroit Pistons the same night.

articles.title: Enes Kanter Freedom goes scorched Earth on LeBron James, NBA with new revelations after WNBA Finals incident
articles.summary: Enes Kanter Freedom alleges Dennis Schröder questioned LeBron James' activism motives and says Boston Celtics teammates shunned him over Fox News.
articles.body: Enes Kanter Freedom has come forward with new allegations regarding the culture of the NBA during his playing career and sent a warning to the WNBA amid his ongoing feud regarding the league's gender eligibility policy. Freedom's new statements come one day after the WNBA tried to direct him to sit in a private luxury suite at Game 3 of the WNBA Finals in Atlanta instead of the courtside seat he purchased, amid security concerns. The change in arrangement resulted in a highly-publicized encounter with police at the entrance of State Farm Arena, which resulted in Freedom leaving the venue entirely amid disagreements over where he wanted to sit. Now Freedom is revealing that his former Boston Celtics teammate Dennis Schröder privately questioned LeBron James’ motives as an activist, and that his Celtics teammates once shunned him for making an appearance on Fox News in his final year in the league in 2021. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! According to Freedom, he asked Schröder that season what James was like as a teammate and how he viewed James’ public advocacy. "He said, 'Whatever is LeBron doing is for LeBron.' I was like, enough said. We don't have to say a word anymore. Because, uh, I used to respect him a lot, you know, uh, for what he'd done for Black community. Uh, but when one of his former teammates said, you know, all his advocacy is for, is for LeBron, um, that's where, that's where he lost me." Freedom also criticized James’ conduct during the national anthem before Philadelphia’s season opener against the Knicks on Tuesday. Video showed James making apparent golf and shooting motions during the performance, prompting criticism from President Donald Trump on Thursday. "But I mean, everybody knows LeBron James... I call him the dictator of the NBA. And I think President Trump said the best. You know, he disrespects our country and disrespects our flag," Freedom said. "LeBron James is the reason the NBA is woke still. I promise you, once he retires, NBA is not going to be as woke as now." In terms of the league's "woke" culture, Freedom also recalled an incident in his final year when he was praised for doing a television appearance on CNN, but shunned for going on Fox News to discuss the same topic of human rights abuses in China. "I actually attended a show on CNN. The next day I walk in the locker room, they were saying, 'Good job last night, we watched your interview, keep doing what you're doing," he said. "The next morning I walk in the locker room, nobody said a word to me. They were not even looking at me. I was getting these dirty looks. I asked one of my teammates, I'm like, what happened?" Freedom said a teammate explained that the objection was to the outlet carrying his message. NBA STAYS SILENT ON WNBA FINALS TEAMS SKIPPING THE NATIONAL ANTHEM BEFORE GAMES 1 AND 2 "They said, well, we watched your interview again last night. I'm like, okay. It's not your interviews, it's who you did it with. I walk on the court, one of my assistant coaches came up to me and whisper— he was whispering in my ear, hey man, me and my family watched you last night, good job. I'm like, why are you whispering?" According to Freedom, the coach feared a backlash of his own. "He said, because I don't want your teammates to know that I watch Fox News. I was like, why? They said, well, because none of them will talk to me the rest of the year." Freedom said he explained to teammates that appearing on the network did not mean endorsing a political party, and that he wanted his human rights advocacy to reach a wider audience. But they weren't receptive to that reasoning, he claims. "In NBA circles, we don't talk about Fox News, we don't watch Fox News, and if you do, you will realize that you are going to get cancelled and you're going to get hated on," Freedom said. But Freedom also claimed that those beliefs are different in private, for some, claiming that that some players privately support conservative causes and President Donald Trump but conceal those views because they fear how they would be treated. But Freedom claimed some NBA players privately support conservative causes and Trump while concealing those views because they fear how others would treat them. "But there are many people actually that supports the conservative movements, supports the Republican Party, uh, many of them actually supports President Trump, but just because of they know that they will get canceled and they will get hated on throughout the whole year, they're just hiding it. I mean, you're not even allowed to say you watch Fox News," Freedom said. GOP CONGRESSMAN PRESSES WNBA TO DEFINE ‘WOMEN’ AFTER ENES KANTER FREEDOM, ROYCE WHITE RULED INELIGIBLE Freedom said he has encountered similar reluctance to speak publicly among former NBA colleagues discussing his current campaign to push the WNBA to explicitly restrict eligibility to biological females. He said some initially questioned his tactics, but expressed support after he explained his intentions. "I don't want to give their name because I know, I just know that as soon as I expose their name, then there will be a lot of questions," Freedom said. According to Freedom, those conversations included players telling him "we cannot help you," while also saying, "but now we understand what you're doing and we support you and we will pray for you." Freedom also pointed to a podcast conversation with Michael Porter Jr., saying Porter initially had questions about the campaign and understood his position better after they discussed it. He did not identify the other players he said privately supported him. Meanwhile, Freedom named Kevin Durant, Patrick Beverley, Matt Barnes and Stephen Jackson among the current and former NBA players he said have criticized him, challenging them to discuss their disagreements directly. "Invite me to your podcast and let's sit down and talk. And let me explain to you why am I doing the things that I'm doing. Don't just go on Twitter. Don't just go on social media and just tweet about it. You know how to, you know, you have my number." His campaign to join the WNBA has now culminated in two hostile incidents at WNBA arenas after he was ejected from a Chicago Sky game in August, and then faced police resistance while trying to enter State Farm Arena on Wednesday night. Freedom said one of the reasons that sitting courtside on Wednesday was so important to him was because he wanted to make sure that his shirt, which read "What is a woman?" would be as visible as possible during the game. Asked whether he wanted television cameras to capture his "What is a woman?" shirt from courtside, he acknowledged that visibility was part of his thinking. "I mean, that was one of the reasons maybe. My main reason was I wanted to support the WNBA," he said. But he said accepting the suite was never an option. "They were trying to put me in a prison box. And I mean, everyone knows me that I'm not going to bow down or kneel to someone who is trying to silence me," Freedom said. The Atlanta Dream and State Farm Arena said the arrangement responded to safety concerns Freedom himself had raised with authorities and basketball officials. They said the suite would have additional security and was intended to protect him and other guests. Although Freedom objected to being surrounded by police at the entrance, he acknowledged that the officers treated him courteously. "They were very, actually very kind. They were trying to do their job, and I was being very very nice to them as well," he said. "This is not their fault." He nevertheless rejected suggestions that he should have accepted the seating arrangement or handled the encounter more diplomatically. "I think I handled everything perfectly," he said. Freedom also pushed back against accusations that his campaign is a publicity stunt, pointing to threats he said included references to Charlie Kirk’s shooting. "I think people need to understand I'm getting death threats every hour. I mean, I showed you that the text messages, you know, yesterday that people are sending me pictures and videos of the moment that Charlie Kirk got shot and said, you are next," he said. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE "So I'm not that crazy. I'm not going to put my life on risk just to get attention." Freedom said the campaign would end if the WNBA explicitly restricted eligibility to biological females. The league has already declared Freedom and fellow former NBA player Royce White ineligible, while its collective bargaining agreement limits participation to women without specifying sex assigned at birth. "I'm literally telling the league that define what a woman is, or add the word biological in your collective bargaining next to the word female. I will disappear the next day," Freedom said. But he said he was finished initiating further discussions with league officials. "If they would like to sit down and have a conversation with me, listen, I love diplomacy," he said. "But I'm done reaching out. So if they would like to reach out, uh, go ahead. You have my number." Despite the league’s eligibility determination, Freedom said he still intends to attend the next draft and continue preparing for it. He also claimed the campaign could expand to include additional male professional players, whom he did not identify. "If they don't draft me and if they don't change the rules, now they have to deal with 6 other male professional players," he said. articles.title: LeBron James Responds to President Trump's Criticism of His Routine During National Anthem
articles.summary: Philadelphia 76ers star LeBron James responded Thursday night to a social media post from United States President Donald Trump demanding an apology for seemingly warming up during the national anthem ahead of Tuesday night's season opener against the New York Knicks.
articles.body:
Philadelphia 76ers star LeBron James responded Thursday night to a social media post from United States President Donald Trump demanding an apology for seemingly warming up during the national anthem ahead of Tuesday night's season opener against the New York Knicks.

"Must've been a slow news day at the office," James told reporters after the Sixers claimed a 114-106 win in their home opener against the Cleveland Cavaliers.

James made his Sixers debut Tuesday on the road against the defending champion Knicks.

The NBA's all-time leading scorer could be seen miming what appeared to be golf swings and jump shots as the national anthem played at Madison Square Garden ahead of the 76ers' 106-100 win.

Trump responded with a post in which he called James a "total disgrace" who "disrespects our country."

He continued to criticize James in a Thursday night campaign rally in Sioux City, Iowa.

Sixers coach Nick Nurse said ahead of Thursday's win he saw Trump's criticism as something "that goes right in with other outside noise we've already had."

"All I really care about is getting them to the practice floor, getting them in the film room, getting them to the game floor, and the focus that they've had and the intent and all the stuff they've had has been excellent," Nurse said.

James has averaged 15.5 points and 9.5 rebounds across his first two games with the Sixers, who are looking to improve to 3-0 Saturday night against the visiting Milwaukee Bucks.

articles.title: SGA Reacts to Historic 20-Point Game Streak Ending, 'Always Treat the Game with Respect'
articles.summary: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander says he snapped his NBA record streak of consecutive 20-point games in Thursday night's home opener win over the Denver Nuggets because he saw it as a measure of "respect" not to play against his opponents' bench in a blowout.
articles.body:
Shai Gilgeous-Alexander says he snapped his NBA record streak of consecutive 20-point games in Thursday night's home opener win over the Denver Nuggets because he saw it as a measure of "respect" not to play against his opponents' bench in a blowout.

Gilgeous-Alexander asked to be subbed out of Thursday's 96-84 victory with just 17 points, snapping a historic 141-game regular-season streak that stretched back to October 2024.

"I was going to go out there, and I saw that they had subbed, so I was just like, 'We should sub, too,'" Gilgeous-Alexander told reporters after the win.

"I feel like you always treat the game with respect. God willing, I have many more games to start another streak, so it's not the end of the world."

Thunder coach Mark Daigneault previously said Gilgeous-Alexander had "asked out of the game" after the Nuggets called a timeout 1:43 remaining in the fourth.

The Nuggets, who were trailing by 17 points at the time, used the same break to sub out their own starting lineup.

"He's got a historic streak going... the class that it shows, and the perspective that it shows, for him to say, 'Hey, I'm out now. The game's calling for me to be subbed out of the game,'" Daigneault said.

"Of all of the things that I admire about him, that's towards the top of the list in terms of moments that I appreciate about him. It shows tremendous class as a competitor."

The Thunder trailed early as Gilgeous-Alexander missed his first seven shots but later recovered to lead a dominant third-quarter stretch.

The comeback allowed the Thunder (2-0) to remain undefeated despite a low-efficiency night during which the home team shot just 38 percent from the field and 26 percent from deep.

Gilgeous-Alexander, who went 6-for-19 from the field and 3-for-11 from behind the arc, will look to start a new 20-point game streak with a more efficient performance Sunday against against the visiting Los Angeles Clippers.

articles.title: 76ers' LeBron James Says Cavs Were 'In Consideration For Sure' as NBA Free Agency Landing Spot
articles.summary: LeBron James says he gave "a lot of consideration" to rejoining the Cleveland Cavaliers before signing with the Philadelphia 76ers this offseason.
articles.body:
LeBron James says he gave "a lot of consideration" to rejoining the Cleveland Cavaliers before signing with the Philadelphia 76ers this offseason.

James was asked after the Sixers' 114-106 Thursday night comeback win over the visiting Cavaliers about a reported meeting between James and the Cleveland front office in early July.

"The nature of the meeting, I probably won't discuss much, but it was in consideration for sure," James told reporters Thursday night (h/t PHLY Sports ).

"It was just a team that's trying to build towards a championship, and things of that nature, and I was trying to decide where I wanted to go with the rest of my career... a lot of consideration, for sure."

ESPN's Shams Charania initially mentioned on a July episode of agent Rich Paul's Game Over podcast James had recently met with Cavaliers president Koby Altman, general manager Brandon Weems and owners from the Gilbert family in his hometown Akron, Ohio.

Paul responded by asking how Charania knew about the meeting (h/t BasketNews ).

Cavaliers coach Kenny Atkinson confirmed in mid-July the Cavaliers were "in the mix" to sign James.

James instead signed later that month with the Sixers on a two-year, $8 million deal with a player option.

The NBA's all-time leading scorer played two previous stints in Cleveland, including the first seven seasons of his NBA career and a return run that resulted in the franchise's first title in 2016.

After recording a double-double against the Cavs Thursday night, James is now looking to lead the Sixers, who haven't won a championship since 1983, on a similar resurgence during his first season in Philadelphia.

articles.title: Joel Embiid Says Past 76ers Teams Would've 'Laid Down' After Historic Comeback vs. Cavs
articles.summary: Philadelphia 76ers star Joel Embiid feels his team's historic Thursday night comeback against the Cleveland Cavaliers is proof of a new team identity in Philly.
articles.body:
Philadelphia 76ers star Joel Embiid feels his team's historic Thursday night comeback against the Cleveland Cavaliers is proof of a new team identity in Philly.

The Sixers, who got booed by their home crowd after falling into a 29-point hole in Thursday's first half, launched the franchise's largest comeback of the play-by-play era to secure a 114-106 win over the Cavs.

"No shade to anybody that's been here, but in the past, a lot of people would've just laid down and tried to move on to the next one," Embiid told reporters .

"We've got the talent. I would like for us to not be in that position again, in the first place, so we don't have to do it every night, because that takes a lot of energy. But yeah, it was different. I said it last game, after the game. It just feels different."

Sixers head coach Nick Nurse said after the game his players were angry to be facing a 69-45 deficit heading into the halftime break.

"The voices at halftime were like, 'Still a game. Settle down and let's start playing our game,'" Nurse said. "They were pissed. They were down and pissed, both. Getting over what just happened, kind of realizing, 'Oh my god, we've got to snap out of it.'"

The Sixers had cut the Cavs' lead to eight points by the end of the third quarter before outscoring the visitors 31-16 in the fourth to claim the win.

Tyrese Maxey led his team with 32 points, while Embiid and Jaylen Brown both topped 20. LeBron James contributed a 17-point, 10-rebound double-double in his Sixers home debut to help secure the largest comeback of his 24-year NBA career.

After opening the season by with a win over the defending champion New York Knicks and the historic comeback over the Cavs, the Sixers will look to keep the momentum going as the season continues Saturday night against the visiting Milwaukee Bucks.

articles.title: LeBron James Reacts to Donald Trump Blasting Him Over National Anthem
articles.summary: It came hours after Trump shared a post on Truth Social criticizing the NBA star.
articles.body:
LeBron James finally broke his silence regarding criticism from President Donald Trump , who called out his behavior during the national anthem ahead of the Philadelphia 76ers and New York Knicks game at Madison Square Garden earlier in the week.

Speaking to reporters on Thursday night during a press conferenc e after the game, which saw the 76ers beat the Cleveland Cavaliers in a 114-106 comeback victory, James brushed off the controversy with a brief response: "It's a slow news day at the office, you know. Slow news day in the office."

The tension began after Trump shared a video on Truth Social just hours before, which showed James practicing a golf swing and a jump shot while the anthem played, while his 76ers teammates mostly stood still.

In the post, Trump slammed the four-time NBA champion as a "TOTAL DISGRACE" and demanded an apology for American veterans and heroes who died for the flag.

Trump's remarks add another chapter to a long-running public feud between the two, which spans over a decade of political clashes, critical social media jabs, and James' long history of activism on racial equality and social justice issues.

It dates back to 2017 when James called Trump a "bum" on social media after the White House rescinded an invitation to Stephen Curry and the Golden State Warriors, stating that visiting the nation's capital was a great honor "until you showed up."

On social media, users have responded to the most recent rift between James and Trump. One user commented under one of the posts: "Hilarious thing to say to possibly the most famous athlete in America right before the midterms. Trump is in a class of his own." Another user wrote : "that one liner was actually too smooth, he really just dismissed him like that."

This isn't the first time that athletes have had issues with Trump and his administration. Earlier this year, former Philadelphia Eagles safety Brian Dawkins and the NFL pushed back against the Department of Homeland Security after the agency used unauthorized footage of the retired athlete in a post about immigration and enforcement efforts.

76ers head coach Nick Nurse addressed the media before Thursday night's game, but chose instead to focus on basketball. Nurse said that the social media storm was part of the " outside noise " that comes with being a famous athlete and said that his team's focus remains on game preparation.

Trump has been campaigning ahead of the midterms elections making stops in Kansas, North Carolina, South Carolina, and Iowa this week. Meanwhile, James' response makes it clear he intends to keep his attention on the game as he navigates a new team with the 2026-27 NBA season underway.

articles.title: How UC Bearcats Week 8 matchup with Brendan Sorsby fell apart
articles.summary: As Texas Tech travels to face Cincinnati, here's a look back at why Brendan Sorbsy won't face his former program after his split with the Red Raiders.
articles.body:
Who has led Cincinnati Bearcats football over for past 80 years?

When the Big 12 released its 2026 football schedule, Week 8 immediately stood out for Cincinnati fans. The Bearcats were set to host Texas Tech and former quarterback Brendan Sorsby after his transfer to the Red Raiders .

Sorsby transferred after two seasons at Cincinnati , and was one of the most sought-after prospects in the portal. He ultimately landed with the Red Raiders , who were coming off a 2025 College Football Playoff berth. His decision to leave the Bearcats prompted the university to sue Sorsby for a $1 million buyout after he allegedly violated his multi-year NIL revenue-sharing agreement.

Of course, Sorsby's reunion with Cincinnati is no longer in play — and not because of an injury.

Sorsby is no longer on Texas Tech's roster after he and Texas Tech mutually agreed to part ways following a high-profile NCAA gambling investigation involving the former Indiana and Cincinnati signal-caller.

Here's what to know about why Sorsby left Texas Tech before the season even started:

Why is Brendan Sorsby no longer on Texas Tech's roster?

Sorsby and Texas Tech parted ways on June 15 after the Big 12 Conference filed a federal lawsuit in Dallas seeking the authority to sanction the school if he played for the Red Raiders. The move came after a Texas judge granted Sorsby a temporary injunction that restored his eligibility while he remained under NCAA investigation related to a gambling addiction.

"I am grateful for the support from my family, my Tech coaching staff, teammates, the community, and so many others who have encouraged me to address and learn more about this important issue," Sorsby wrote in a post on Instagram. "As my journey continues, I remain fully committed to and focused on being the best I can be, both on and off the field."

Sorsby declared for the 2026 NFL Supplemental Draft, though the league declined to host for the former college quarterback. As it stands, he cannot enter the league until the 2027 draft.

Brendan Sorsby betting controversy, explained

The NCAA in March received a tip about Sorsby's betting activity from an online gambling book, which had been informed by law enforcement.

On April 27 the Red Raiders announced Sorsby was checking himself into a residential treatment program in Arizona for a gambling addiction that dated back to his true freshman season at Indiana in 2022. That season, Sorsby placed bets for the first eight games of the season, when he was a member of the Hoosiers' scout team.

He announced on May 28 that he had completed a 35-day inpatient rehab program in Arizona. The NCAA denied Sorsby's request for reinstatement for the 2026 season on May 26, which led him to file an injunction against the NCAA in Lubbock County.

The injunction revealed that Sorsby had placed more than $90,000 in bets over four years through accounts registered to the names of family members and friends. Those wagers included at least 40 bets on Indiana when he was a member of the Hoosiers, but also included bets placed on professional sports .

The documents also revealed that, since transferring to Texas Tech, Sorsby sent approximately $5,000 through Venmo or Zelle to an unnamed individual who placed bets on his behalf.

College football risers and fallers: BYU is for real. Alabama, Texas in trouble

His injunction to play for Texas Tech was granted on June 8 by Judge Ken Curry of the 99th District Court of Lubbock County: a decision that merely imposed a two-game suspension on Sorsby for Texas Tech's first two games of the season against Abilene Christian and Oregon State.

That decision led to an uproar from across the country, with several athletic directors coming out publicly and stating they would not allow their programs to schedule Texas Tech in future contests. It also led to the Big 12 Conference filing a complaint in federal court seeking a declaratory judgment that would allow the league to enforce its bylaws and potentially sanction Texas Tech should the Red Raiders play Sorsby.

The Big 12 considered sanctioning Texas Tech if it played Sorsby, in turn resulting in a legal threat from Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton if the conference tried to enforce its rules. Attorneys general in Oklahoma, Kansas and Utah responded, saying they would back up the conference, which ultimately sued Texas Tech in a Dallas court.

Eventually, Sorsby and Texas Tech agreed to part ways as he prepared for the NFL supplemental draft. The NFL announced in June it would not hold a supplemental draft in 2026, blocking a path for Sorsby to compete in the NFL in 2026.

Is Cincinnati under investigation by the NCAA for Brendan Sorbsy?

No. The NCAA inquiry into University of Cincinnati Athletics regarding Sorsby's gambling was closed on Sept. 2 with no punishments issued to the Bearcats.

Sorsby's agent, Ron Slavin, claimed in a Dallas radio interview in June that Cincinnati knew about Sorsby's gambling activity and did not act on it. Cincinnati, however, denied the accusation, saying in a statement that had it known of any impermissible gambling, it would have reported it to the NCAA.

"Earlier this summer, NCAA enforcement staff completed an inquiry into a former Cincinnati student-athlete's prohibited betting activity during his time at the university. The inquiry is now closed, and the student-athlete was found to have committed a Level III violation," UC Senior Associate Athletic Director for Communications Zach Stipe said in a statement to The Cincinnati Enquirer, part of the USA TODAY Network, on Sept. 2.
